items.caption: This oracle-script style redraw presents an early form of 喜. The upper element is identified as 壴, an early drum graph, above 口; the proposed association with drumming and singing is an interpretation of the graph, not a meaning directly visible in its strokes.
items.alt: Black oracle-script style character form, identified as 喜, with a tall branched upper portion above a rounded lower enclosure containing a short horizontal stroke.
items.selection_reason: It offers a useful visual comparison for the reported oracle-bone forms and the proposed 壴-and-口 analysis. The drum-and-singing interpretation is scholarly, and the cited early examples have no secure absolute dates here.

items.caption: This small-seal style redraw shows 喜 with a branched upper element above a rounded middle enclosure and a larger lower enclosure. Shuowen analyzes the graph as 壴 and 口, though that historical account does not independently confirm the proposed motivation.
items.alt: Black small-seal style character identified as 喜, with three stacked sections: a branched upper form, a rounded central enclosure, and a broad lower enclosure.
items.selection_reason: It provides a distinct script-style comparison alongside the oracle-script redraw and relates to the graph analysis preserved in Shuowen. The image is a modern redraw, not an artifact image.

limitations.text: The drum-and-singing explanation is a proposed account of the graph’s motivation. Other interpretations have been offered, and the reported oracle-bone examples include both joy and name uses without secure dates that establish their order.

Both illustrations are modern redrawings of script styles, not photographs of inscribed objects. Their labels identify the represented styles, but they do not by themselves establish a dated sequence of forms.
